title: The Reform School Billionaire
lines: This trillion-dollar CEO was sent to reform school. By mistake.
Jensen Huang runs Nvidia, the company powering nearly every AI on Earth. But his story starts with a mistake that should have broken him.
Born in Taiwan. Raised in Thailand. At nine, his parents send him and his brother to America, alone. His uncle picks what he thinks is an elite boarding school.
It wasn't. Oneida Baptist Institute was a reform school in rural Kentucky. His roommate was seventeen, covered in tattoos and knife scars. Jensen's job? Cleaning the toilets. Every single day.
But he didn't break. He taught that roommate to read. In return, the roommate taught him to lift. Later, he said those years made him tough.
At fifteen, he's washing dishes at a Denny's in Oregon. In 1993, in a Denny's booth in San Jose, he and two friends start Nvidia.
Three years later, the first chip flops. Half the staff is gone. Nvidia is about thirty days from dying. One last chip saves it.
Today it's worth trillions. So his biggest secret isn't a chip. It's that he scrubbed toilets before he got here.
